newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya opposition wary over government reform bill.
newsitem.headline: Kenya opposition wary over government reform bill.

text.p: Kenya's opposition said on Saturday it was deeply suspicious of a government reform and anti-corruption bill and argued it did not go far enough.
Attorney-General Amos Wako published on Friday "The Statute Law (Repeals and Miscellaneous Act) Bill 1997" for debate and approval by parliament.
He also proposed amending various laws ranging from banking to public security and repeal of the Vagrancy Act under which police can detain anyone on suspicion of being a vagabond.

"He (Wako) has not moved far enough and one can see that (President Daniel arap Moi) and Wako have perfected this act of testing the waters and seeing how much they can get away with," said opposition leader Paul Muite, a member of parliament and an activist in the unregistered Safina party.
"They have no intention of levelling the playing field to make the election free and fair," Muite said.

The ruling Kenya African National Union (KANU) recommended last month repeal of 11 controversial laws and the establishment before elections due later this year of a commission to review the constitution.
At least nine people died on July 7 when security forces moved against rallies by an opposition-backed campaign for constitutional reform.

The International Monetary Fund on Thursday halted a multi-million-dollar aid package for Kenya, turning down Kenya's request for more time to try to take measures to meet IMF concerns about corruption and its demand for the reform of the energy sector.
